title: Deep earthquakes had a larger M6.5+ share after cell and preferred-method matching in selected ComCat data for 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether exact preferred magnitude method mix explains a deep-minus-intermediate size-share contrast in ComCat for 2000-2025. We matched 15 method-cell strata in nine 20-degree cells, with at least ten M5.5+ events in each depth band. The sample retained 873 intermediate and 597 deep events. The fixed-weight M6.5+ shares were 9.27% and 18.79%. The difference was 9.52 percentage points, with a conditional 95% three-year block interval of 4.73 to 14.87 points. Method matching changed the cell-weight estimate on the same records by +0.16 points, with an interval of -1.29 to 2.75 points. Thus the tested method weights did not remove the contrast. Only moment methods had common support. The late-era estimate was undefined on the full-period support because some method strata had no events. Method selection, within-cell geography, catalog errors, time changes and conditional uncertainty prevent a causal depth claim. This extends prior campaign work with the same observations, not independent confirmation. Code, aggregate counts, draw results, source hashes, a figure and arithmetic checks are included. External event records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Deep-minus-intermediate large-event shares after cell and exact preferred-method weights. Intervals are conditional on fixed support. The paired change from cell weights includes zero.
